target_customer: Chinese-speaking students and early career workers who pay for digital skills training aimed at US and Chinese tech jobs
problem: Chinese-speaking learners lack practical, job-linked training in digital marketing, data analytics and product design. CareerTu taught them with capstone projects and connected them with employers.
business_model: Paid courses to students, with recruiting partners

founders.name: Ruiwan Xu
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says she started blogging and grew it into an online school; the article reports a six-year-old business.

founders.name: Qian Qiao
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

founders.name: Yvonne Tian
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

competitors.name: Udacity
competitors.what: Online nanodegrees; its China team served entry-level coders, data analysts and digital marketers

technical_complexity.rationale: Course delivery over WeChat and a web platform is ordinary engineering; the value is in curriculum and employer links.

defensibility.rationale: Employer partnerships and the WeChat audience helped, but courseware and credentials are easy for platforms like Udacity and Coursera to offer.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported about 160,000 users, 500 recruiting partners and 6,000 paying users with roughly $500,000 revenue in the prior year, and growth in China traffic.

branding.domain_note: Uses careertu.com; it is now a GoDaddy Launching Soon placeholder page (fetched 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: TechCrunch framed it as Codecademy for digital marketing.

branding.community_and_virality: Audience reached through a WeChat official account and a blog, per Crunchbase and TechCrunch coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: A WeChat audience of 160,000 users and a TechCrunch profile, but no brand assets or fan activity found.

outcome_analysis: CareerTu was already a profitable roughly six-year-old education business with about $500,000 in annual revenue when it joined YC in Winter 2019, then raised about $150K. YC lists it inactive and the website is now a Launching Soon placeholder. No shutdown report or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public; China's 2021 edtech crackdown is context but not tied to this company by any source, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Investors AvanTech Ventures and VentureSouq come from a CB Insights search snippet (single database), while the amount and YC investment are in TechCrunch. CB Insights says founded 2013, Bounce Watch 2018, and TechCrunch says six-year-old business in 2019; 2018 is the YC page value. Competitor list has one dated source; TechCrunch compared it to Codecademy as an analogy, not a named rival.
